note: An ear game of the 2nds and 3rds, sometimes an octave wider (the 9th and the 10th), named as the simple interval as the game's buttons show them; the why says how to fold a wide leap back into one octave. Tagged multi-octave, one feel to reach.

exercise.title: Leaps wider than an octave
exercise.why: A 9th is a 2nd with an octave added and a 10th is a 3rd with an octave added, so bring the top note down an octave in your head and the leap you know is there.

cells.text:
Press Start below to hear the first question: the game plays Do, then a note a 2nd or a 3rd above it, sometimes an octave further up.
When the top note is far away, hum it an octave lower. Then pick its name: M2 for the major 2nd, m3 for the minor 3rd, M3 for the major 3rd, and press Next below for another leap: the answer is the same with or without the extra octave.
Practice until you bring the top note down an octave without humming it.
